entries.title: [Series] The changing therapeutic landscape of small-cell lung cancer
entries.description: Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an exceptionally aggressive malignancy: highly proliferative, heterogeneous, and frequently metastatic at diagnosis. Although initially responsive to chemotherapy, such responses are typically transient, and recurrent disease has been largely refractory to standard cytotoxics. The past decade has been notable for major advances in our understanding of SCLC biology, and this preclinical progress is now informing multiple novel therapeutic approaches for this disease.

entries.title: The ice blasting from Saturn's moon Enceladus is stranger than scientists realized
entries.description: Enceladus may naturally separate and concentrate chemicals from its hidden ocean as droplets slowly freeze and shatter on their way into space. The process could explain Cassini’s puzzling ice-grain chemistry while giving future spacecraft a powerful advantage in searching for organic compounds and clues to life.

entries.title: Caltech’s tiny new chip can steer light in 74 quadrillionths of a second
entries.description: A new Caltech device can redirect a beam of light in just 74 femtoseconds using another beam and a nanoscale silicon metasurface. The breakthrough could pave the way for dramatically faster photonic communications, computing, and sensing technologies.

entries.title: UN panel calls for stronger safeguards as AI agents advance
entries.description: The world's first scientific body on Artificial Intelligence called on Monday for AI safeguards to be adapted as current firewalls are “unravelling”.

entries.title: ADB Approves $100 Million Loan to Boost Skills Development and Jobs for Youth in Sri Lanka
entries.description: ADB has approved a $100 million results-based loan to help Sri Lanka transform its technical and vocational education and training system, equip more young people with industry-relevant skills, and strengthen the country's competitiveness and inclusive growth.

entries.title: ADB Approves $400 Million Loan to Support Earthquake Recovery, Expand SME Access to Finance in Türkiye
entries.description: ADB has approved a $400 million loan to Türkiye Vakıflar Bankası T.A.O. to support Türkiye’s post-earthquake recovery by building disaster-resilient houses, promoting clean energy, and expanding access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises owned by or employing women in less developed provinces.

entries.title: ADB, Modern Syntex Sign $50 Million Loan to Expand Energy-Efficient Polyester Chips Production in Bangladesh
entries.description: ADB and Modern Syntex Limited have signed a $50 million loan for the Modern Energy-Efficient Polyester Chips Manufacturing Project in Bangladesh.

entries.title: ADB Approves $100 Million Loan to Expand Access to Affordable, Resilient Housing Finance in Bangladesh
entries.description: ADB has approved a $100 million concessional loan to expand access to affordable and resilient housing finance for low- and middle-income borrowers in Bangladesh, particularly women.

entries.title: ADB Launches $6 Billion Push for Healthier Seas and Coastal Economies
entries.description: ADB has announced it will mobilize up to $6 billion through 2030 to confront the mounting threats facing Southeast Asia’s seas and strengthen the blue economy that the region’s food supplies, jobs, and trade depend on.

entries.title: ADB Approves $3 Million Grant to Address Violence Against Women and Children in Mongolia through Safer Schools and Stronger Support Services
entries.description: ADB has approved a $3 million grant to help Mongolia prevent and respond to violence against women and children through safer schools, improved survivor support services, and effective policy reforms.

entries.title: ADB Approves $175 Million Loan to Modernize Power Networks, Boost Jobs and Services in Bangladesh’s Chattogram Hill Tracts
entries.description: ADB has approved a $175 million concessional loan to expand access to reliable and affordable electricity in Bangladesh’s Chattogram Hill Tracts, helping boost livelihoods, improve essential services, and support inclusive development in one of the country’s most remote regions.

entries.title: CAREC Marks 25 Years with Over $60 Billion in Investment
entries.description: The Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) Program marked its 25th anniversary today with $60.2 billion in cumulative investment, having grown from five founding countries into an 11-country partnership.

entries.title: ADB Supports Fiscal Reforms for Stronger Public Service Delivery in Indonesia
entries.description: ADB has approved a $650 million equivalent program to help Indonesia modernize intergovernmental fiscal management, advance digital governance, and improve public service delivery across the country’s decentralized system of government.

entries.title: ADB Expands Access to Quality Education in Mongolia
entries.description: ADB has approved a $130 million loan to reduce overcrowding and improve access to quality education in Mongolia.

entries.title: ADB Launches New Country Partnership Strategy to Support Growth in Papua New Guinea
entries.description: ADB has launched a new 5-year country partnership strategy for Papua New Guinea to support stronger public finances, wider transport and energy connections, and better access to health, education, and other essential services.

entries.title: ADB Sells $5 Billion Dual-Tranche 3- and 7-Year Global Benchmark Bonds
entries.description: ADB has priced a 3-year global benchmark United States dollar bond worth $3 billion and a 7-year global benchmark US dollar bond worth $2 billion, proceeds of which will become part of ADB’s ordinary capital resources.

entries.title: ADB Signs Private Sector Deal to Strengthen Mongolia's Cashmere Value Chain, Create Inclusive Jobs
entries.description: ADB has signed a combined $30 million loan (in togrog equivalent) with Gobi Joint Stock Company (Gobi), Tavan Bogd Foods LLC (TBF), and Tavan Bogd Foods Pizza LLC (TBFP) to strengthen Mongolia's cashmere value chain and expand employment opportunities in the country’s burgeoning food service sector.

entries.title: ADB Supports Mongolia's First Green-Certified Residential Complex Built by the Private Sector
entries.description: ADB has signed a $30 million loan (in togrog equivalent) with Tavan Bogd Holdings LLC to finance the construction of Mongolia's first green-certified residential complex developed by the private sector.

entries.title: ADB Approves $400 Million Financing Facility to Modernize Borders, Facilitate Trade in CAREC Region
entries.description: ADB has approved a $400 million regional financing facility to modernize border crossing points, lower transport and logistics costs, and improve the movement of people and goods across the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) region.

entries.title: ADB and Partners Launch Initiative to Scale Financing for Land Degradation and Desertification in Asia and the Pacific
entries.description: ADB has launched together with partners the Financing Investments and Eradicating Land Degradation and Desertification Initiative, a regional partnership to attract at least $2 billion by 2035 to invest in programs that restore lands and strengthen drought resilience across Asia and the Pacific.

entries.title: ADB Approves Project to Expand Access to Life-Saving Care in Mongolia’s Provinces
entries.description: ADB has approved a $225 million loan—its largest health sector investment in Mongolia—to expand access to quality health care across the country’s provinces through major upgrades in health infrastructure, emergency care, digital health systems, medical equipment, and workforce capacity.

entries.title: Clean your plate – to reduce food loss and waste
entries.description: Food waste is helping to fuel global warming, one half-eaten sandwich at a time.

entries.title: Right to development: A blueprint for unmet promises
entries.description: Ahead of the 40th anniversary of the groundbreaking Declaration on the Right to Development this December, world leaders gathered at a High-Level Week meeting on Wednesday to map progress made and the 21st century challenges still ahead – from narrowing the digital divide to levelling the AI playing field – as the UN chief presented a “blueprint” to address promises that remain unfulfilled.

entries.title: Is organic farming better for the environment than conventional farming?

entries.title: ADB and Republic of Korea Deepen Ties on Energy, Critical Minerals, and Artificial Intelligence

entries.title: ADB Strengthens Partnership with Indonesia-Malaysia-Thailand Growth Triangle on Connectivity, Resilience

entries.description: ADB's private sector financing increased by 38% in 2025 to $9.5 billion, including $900 million in long-term direct mobilization for transaction advisory services, according to the Private Sector Operations in 2025 Report on Development Effectiveness.

entries.description: The Security Council met Monday morning with prospects for peace in the Middle East under strain on two fronts. In the West Bank, settler violence and settlement expansion are raising fears for a two-State solution. In Gaza, a year-old peace plan has stalled while civilian suffering continues. entries.title: UN hails Libya election deal as Security Council urges Libyans to seize the moment
entries.description: The UN Security Council has welcomed a breakthrough agreement between Libya's rival political blocs, calling it "an important step" towards the country's first national elections in over a decade – while pressing all sides to move quickly from paper to practice.

entries.title: New initiative launched to shield terrorism victims from online harm

entries.title: At SCO summit In Kyrgyzstan, Guterres calls for more representative global governance
entries.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Tuesday urged leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) to help reshape global governance for a changing world, arguing that a more multipolar international order can strengthen multilateralism, advance fairness and better serve developing countries.

entries.title: Aid reaches hundreds of thousands in Gaza amid severe food insecurity

entries.title: Explainer: UN peace operations work to create, preserve peace
entries.description: Supporting the first democratic elections after brutal civil wars in Mozambique and Cambodia. Disarming thousands of child soldiers in Sierra Leone. Helping to secure Namibia’s independence from South Africa. These are some of the contributions of UN operations around the world to help countries transition from conflict to lasting peace.

entries.title: Security Council LIVE: Drone strikes and political impasse in Libya
entries.description: As Libya faces a political impasse delaying long-planned elections alongside clashes and drone strikes that left a major oil refinery ablaze, the Security Council heard the latest updates, with an activist warning that the collision of extreme heat, water scarcity and environmental shocks with political division, armed insecurity and struggling institutions clearly makes the situation a peace and security issue. entries.title: FLEX and Sentinel-3C launched

entries.title: A team of teams like never before: rehearsing a unique launch at ESA mission control
entries.description: On 15 September, two spacecraft will leave Earth together aboard the same launcher from Europe’s spaceport in Kourou: FLEX, ESA’s photosynthesis mission, and Sentinel-3C, Copernicus’ newest satellite monitoring Earth’s oceans, land, ice and atmosphere. At ESA’s European Space Operations Centre (ESOC), two independent mission teams are preparing to operate the spacecraft in parallel in a closely coordinated effort. As launch approaches, they are rehearsing side by side to prepare not only for their own missions, but also for the moments when the two operations intersect.
